**Triage: lands across the object-metadata write call sites and the objectui#7714 guards; `domain:ui`; `priority:p2`.**

objectui#7714's ruling **enumerated two writers** and its PR guarded both. The card swept and found **12 of 15 call sites route through neither guard** — and, the part that outlives the count, **a `client.save(` sweep cannot see them**, so the natural probe under-reports the population by construction.

⇒ p2: an integrity guard covering 3 of 15 write paths is a guard in name. ⚠️ It is not p1 because this is a coverage gap rather than a demonstrated bad write — ⛔ but if the taking dev finds a reachable path where an unguarded write corrupts stored metadata, **say so and re-price it** rather than landing quietly at p2.

### ⭐ The durable half — carry it into the fix

> a ruling that enumerates writers is only as good as the enumeration.

⇒ ⛔ **Do not fix this by hand-enumerating 15 writers.** That reproduces objectui#7714's failure with a bigger list. **Derive the write set**, or place the guard where every writer must pass through it. A hand list is stale the next time someone adds a writer, and nothing will say so.

⚠️ Take the census fresh — the card's 12-of-15 is from 2026-09-08 and the tree has moved. Report the numbers you measure, ⛔ not the card's.

`Size/model suggestion:` M–L — the guard placement is the design question and it is the whole value.

### Carried into the dispatch, from triage

- ⛔ **Do not fix this by hand-enumerating 15 writers.** That reproduces objectui#7714's failure with a bigger list. **Derive the write set**, or place the guard where every writer must pass through it.
- ⚠️ **Take the census fresh.** The card's 12-of-15 is from 2026-09-08 on `4eb665bcf` and the tree has moved. Report the numbers measured, ⛔ not the card's.
- ⚠️ p2 is a **coverage** grade, not a demonstrated bad write. ⇒ if a reachable path is found where an unguarded write corrupts stored metadata, **say so and re-price it** rather than landing quietly at p2.
- ⭐ The sweep shape the question is naturally asked in (`client.save(`) **cannot see** these call sites. Whatever probe is used, prove it with a lit control before reading any zero off it.

### ⚠️ Neighbour in flight — declared so it is not discovered as a conflict

objectui#8442 is dispatched concurrently and works in `packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx` plus `@object-ui/types`' chat contract. That should be disjoint from the object-metadata write paths, but `app-shell` is one package both can reach. ⇒ merge `origin/main` before finishing, and if the guard's placement pulls it into the AI chat surface, **stop and report** rather than resolving it in the diff.

## Closing — the class is closed at the doors, and the closure is CI-enforced. Measured on `main`

⛔ **Not inherited from the PR.** My release note (2026-09-14T09:26Z) said this seat had not re-measured. I read PR objectui#9238 and measured at `origin/main` `bbc9dc3`.

### ⭐ The card asked for something better than its own fix, and got it

The card's literal finding was *"12 of the 15 object-metadata write call sites route through neither objectui#7714 guard"*. The obvious repair — guard the twelve — is **the very thing the card is a complaint about**:

> objectui#7714's ruling names two writers and its PR guards both … ⇒ **is there a fourth?** A ruling that enumerates writers is only as good as the enumeration.

objectui#7714 enumerated two. objectui#8057 found a third **in that card's own required dogfood**. This card's sweep found nine more. ⇒ guarding twelve would have made this the fourth card in the series.

**What landed instead moves the invariant to the transport.** `packages/data-objectstack/src/object-metadata-write-guard.ts:152` declares `assertObjectMetadataWritable`, and it is applied at the three doors bytes actually leave through:

| door | site |
|---|---|
| the generic SDK save | `packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts:955` — `assertObjectMetadataWritable(type, item, 'MetadataClient.save')` |
| the app-shell service | `packages/app-shell/src/services/MetadataService.ts:656` |
| the hand-rolled `fetch` PUT | `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/external/api.ts:195` — `importObjectDraft` |

⇒ **the twelve call sites are untouched and now guarded anyway**, which is the point. They still spell `client.save<T>(type, …)`; that call now passes through the guard by construction. A thirteenth writer added tomorrow needs no entry anywhere.

### ⭐⭐ The methodological half — the part I most wanted to check

The card's sharper claim was that **the sweep this question is naturally asked in cannot see its own subject**: `git grep 'client\.save('` returns **0** over `ResourceEditPage.tsx`, the file objectui#8057 is entirely about, because the generic argument sits between the name and the paren. The gate's own docblock answers it in the only way that survives:

> ⇒ So this gate does not enumerate writers, and ⛔ no fix for this class ever should. It enumerates DOORS. … The writer set is OPEN … The door set is CLOSED and this repository owns it … **A list is a claim about the world; this is a measurement of the tree.**

And it names the door that **no `.save`-shaped sweep of any spelling could ever have found** — `importObjectDraft`, a hand-rolled `fetch` PUT to `/api/v1/meta/object/:name`.

### The enforcement, verified rather than assumed

⚠️ A gate that CI never runs is a gate that rots, so this was checked directly and **not** from the PR's word:

- `scripts/check-object-metadata-write-doors.mjs` — the gate.
- `package.json:104` — `"check:metadata-write-doors": "node scripts/check-object-metadata-write-doors.mjs"`.
